title: Canonical image tagging + automated SBOM sync with CUDA/driver compatibility manifest and rollout gates
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Our current image tagging and SBOM publishing are inconsistent across the hosted, dedicated, and private channels. This gap causes confusion during LTS rollouts, and has led to a recent on-call incident where nodes were upgraded to a CUDA driver not compatible with a pinned image (INC-2025-230). Goal: Establish a canonical image-tag lifecycle, ensure every released container image is accompanied by a versioned SBOM and a machine-readable compatibility manifest that pins CUDA/runtime driver ranges. Integrate verification into the release pipeline and implement rollout gates that block automatic promotion if compatibility checks fail.
acceptance_criteria: All release images in the runtime-1.20 channel include a signed SBOM artifact published to artifacts.redwood-infra/storage with matching semantic tag (e.g., runtime:1.20.0+sha256:...),
A compatibility-manifest artifact is generated per image containing: image-tag, build-kernel-ABI, recommended CUDA driver versions, minimum driver version, and tested GPU SKUs
Release pipeline validates that node pools targeted for upgrade have drivers within the manifest's supported range; failing nodes prevent canary promotions
A dashboard shows image -> sbom -> compatibility manifest mapping and final gating status for each rollout
Documentation (Confluence) updated with the tag lifecycle and rollback procedures
implementation_notes: Add a new step to the image build pipeline (images/builder) that runs syft/grype to produce SBOM and stores it alongside the image in the artifact registry

Create a small tool (compat-gen) that reads build metadata and produces the compatibility-manifest JSON; store manifest as an artifact with predictable path: artifacts/runtime/<tag>/compat-manifest.json
Extend the release orchestrator to fetch manifest and run a nodepool-driver-check before promoting from canary to general availability
Pinning strategy: images will carry both semantic version and build metadata; for pinned deployments we will add explicit driver pin labels to node pool configs
Use signed metadata (cosign) for SBOMs and manifests to prevent tampering in Private deployments
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Canary: Release to internal canary account with a single nodepool that we control; gate requires compat-manifest validation
Phase 2 - Extended Canary: Expand to staging customers (5% of traffic) with automated rollback TTL of 30 minutes if health checks degrade
Phase 3 - GA: After 48h of stable metrics, promote to GA; promotion pipeline enforces driver checks across target regions
Manual rollback instructions added to runbook: revert image tag via console or CLI and run nodepool-driver-rollback job
testing_plan: Unit tests for compat-gen produced manifests with mocked build metadata
Integration test in CI that builds an image, publishes SBOM and manifest, then runs the release-orchestrator's validation step in a dry-run mode
Chaos test: simulate nodepool with out-of-range driver and assert pipeline blocks promotion
Post-release smoke: automated end-to-end generation of SBOM+manifest and verification in a pre-prod environment
risks: False negatives: manifests missing required fields could block healthy rollouts if validation is too strict
Private/on-prem customers with locked drivers may require coordination and manual overrides; need clear doc and an approval audit trail
Performance: additional build steps increase image build time by ~3-7 minutes; we must parallelize SBOM creation
Key management: signing SBOMs requires access to KMS; need on-call ops to rotate keys safely
